hardware.variant: One assembled kit with operator-reported CoreBoard V1.2.

inputs.name: ESP_MOSAICO_SC101IOT WDEV RX diagnostic FIT
inputs.revision: Candidate RAM kernel diagnostic d76cb; not a release image.

inputs.name: WPA2-PSK/CCMP/PMF0 profile and selected AP
inputs.revision: Pinned AP0 control trial; identifiers omitted.

scenario: One bounded WPA2-PSK/CCMP/PMF0 control attempt on an operator-reported V1.2 sample, with pinned AP0 and diagnostic observations at the normal STA callback, vendor protocol/sublength boundaries, association-stage register readback, and opaque hardware/allocator counters.
expected: Reach WPA_COMPLETED while checking live diagnostic bindings, observed receive frame-type counts, association-stage register values, native state, and AP log evidence.
observed: The station reached native RUN at RX policy 6 but did not reach WPA_COMPLETED; the supplicant ended in SCANNING and the kernel disconnected with reason 204 after the PTK 4-way handshake timeout. The normal pTxRx table at +0x3f8 matched; sta_rx_cb ran 122 times, all management frames (122/0/0/0). sta_input_table, crypto_decap, decap, and sta_rx_eapol were zero. The pp_wdev_funcs hook at ppRxProtoProc+0x198 matched its live slot; its FC matrix (management/control/data/extension × rxmatch0 clear/set) was 0/122, 0/0, 0/0, 0/0. The sublength hook at pp_wdev_funcs+0x414 and its ROM caller at +0x1f4 matched at begin/end. Its FC matrix was 0/124, 0/0, 0/0, 0/0; invalid and short were zero. The DATA-state histogram prints only nonzero bins; with no observed DATA, no histogram entries were printed, as expected. Association-stage register readback captured valid STA and BSSID values, both matching expected values. BSSID readback did not match outside the association stage during begin/end transitions; this is a phase transition, not an invalid expected address. AP logs recorded two associations, station deauthentication after the PTK timeout, and station disassociation. They do not establish AP transmission or ACK of M1. Hardware getter succeeded; rx_datasuc=124 and other hardware counters are opaque. Allocator misses, fallback, and NULL were zero; window minimum free was 197136 bytes.

measurements.name: disconnect-reason
measurements.unit: local disconnect after PTK 4-way handshake timeout

measurements.name: diagnostic-window
measurements.unit: seconds from debug enable through disconnect

measurements.name: association-register-readback-match
measurements.unit: during association; captured and valid STA/BSSID values matched expected values

measurements.name: transition-bssid-readback-mismatch
measurements.unit: outside association at begin/end; transition readback, not invalid expected value

measurements.name: hardware-rx-datasuc
measurements.unit: opaque hardware counter; not a DATA frame count

limits: One operator-reported V1.2 sample and one RAM-loaded candidate diagnostic kernel; this does not establish support for other revisions or persistent Wi-Fi operation.

The ppRxProtoProc and sublength hooks observe the instrumented software boundaries only; they do not establish all-hardware or over-the-air traffic. No DATA at these boundaries does not determine whether the AP transmitted or where any earlier loss occurred.
The DATA-state histogram prints only nonzero bins. Since the measured DATA count was zero, no histogram entries were emitted; this is the expected empty histogram, not a failed measurement.

Association-stage register readback captured valid STA and BSSID values matching expected values. Begin/end BSSID mismatch occurred outside the association stage during transition and is not an invalid expected value.
AP logs record association and station deauthentication after PTK timeout, not AP transmission or station acknowledgement of M1.
Hardware rx_datasuc and related counters are opaque and do not identify frame type or prove memory pressure. Internal-pool misses, fallback and NULL were zero in this measured window.
No EAPOL input, WPA_COMPLETED, negotiated PMF, IP address, DNS or accepted network data exchange was observed. Wi-Fi support remains partial.
